'''Robert Thomas Patton''' (born October 21, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (American football)|center]] for one season in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played high school football at West Side Central Catholic High School (later Bishop O'Reilly - now closed) in [[Kingston, Pennsylvania]], where he was a teammate of NFL quarterback [[Joe Pisarcik]]. Patton played [[college football]] for the [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens football|Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens]], and he was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 1976. He played in 12 games for the Bills in [[1976 NFL season|1976]]. He retired after one season of playing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Patton Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PattBo20.htm |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Patton played [[college football]] at the [[University of Delaware]] for the [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens football|Fightin' Blue Hens]]. He earned [[United Press International]] All-East honors as an [[offensive guard]] in 1975.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kubacki, McEleney on All-East club |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=xM48AAAAIBAJ&sjid=Ny4MAAAAIBAJ&pg=873,3921161 |newspaper=[[Bangor Daily News]] |date=November 26, 1975 |accessdate=2012-06-17}}</ref> He also earned the Robert C. Peoples Outstanding Senior Lineman award as a senior.<ref>{{cite web |title=All-Time Honors |url=http://www.bluehens.com/teams/football/info/honors.html |publisher=University of Delaware Athletics |accessdate=2012-06-17 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013122900/http://www.bluehens.com/teams/football/info/honors.html |archivedate=2012-10-13 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
The [[Buffalo Bills]] signed Patton as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 20, 1976.<ref>{{cite news |title=Football |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=hHU0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=DhMEAAAAIBAJ&pg=5743,4101434 |newspaper=[[Star-News]] |date=May 20, 1976 |accessdate=2012-06-17}}</ref> He played in 12 games for the Bills in [[1976 NFL season|1976]].

'''Robert Allen Mrosko ''' (born November 13, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for three seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Houston Oilers]], [[New York Giants]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He was selected by the Oilers in the ninth round of the [[1989 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. He was a member of the Giants team that won [[Super Bowl XXV]].

==Early life==
Robert Allen Mrosko was born on November 13, 1965, in [[Cleveland, Ohio]].<ref name="pfa" /> He attended [[Wickliffe High School (Ohio)|Wickliffe High School]] in [[Wickliffe, Ohio]].<ref name="pfa" />

==College career==
Mrosko was a member of the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]] of [[Pennsylvania State University]] from 1984 to 1988.<ref name="pfa">{{Cite web |title=Bob Mrosko |url=https://profootballarchives.com/players/m/mros00200.html |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=profootballarchives.com}}</ref> He [[redshirted]] in 1984 and played sparingly in 1985.<ref name="pfa" /> He was then a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1986 to 1988.<ref name="pfa" /> He caught three passes for 31 yards in 1986.<ref name="sr" /> The [[1986 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|1986 Nittany Lions]] were named consensus national champions. He recorded five receptions for 62 yards in 1987.<ref name="sr">{{Cite web |title=Bob Mrosko |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bob-mrosko-1.html?__hstc=223721476.25eeb56ac40f5746efcdb6231e77d0af.1735305963439.1735305963439.1735315416103.2&__hssc=223721476.1.1735315416103&__hsfp=3011104808 |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=sports-reference.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Mrosko was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] in the ninth round, with the 244th overall pick, of the [[1989 NFL draft]].<ref name="pfr" /> He officially signed with the team on July 11.<ref name="transactions">{{Cite web |title=Bob Mrosko NFL Transactions |url=https://profootballarchives.com/transactions/m/mros00200.html |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=profootballarchives.com}}</ref> He played in 15 games, starting 14, during his rookie season in 1989, catching three passes for 28 yards and returning three kicks for 46 yards.<ref name="pfr" /> The Oilers finished the year with a 9–7 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1989 Houston Oilers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/oti/1989.htm |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> Mrosko also started one playoff game that season.<ref name="pfr" />

Mrosko became a free agent after the 1989 season and signed with the [[New York Giants]] on February 27, 1990.<ref name="transactions" /> He appeared in all 16 games, starting two, for the Giants in 1990, totaling three receptions for 27 yards and one touchdown.<ref name="pfr">{{Cite web |title=Bob Mrosko |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MrosBo00.htm |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> He also played in all three Giants playoff games, starting one, that season, catching one pass for six yards.<ref name="pfr" /> On January 27, 1991, the Giants beat the [[Buffalo Bills]] by a score of 20–19 in [[Super Bowl XXV]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Mrosko 1990 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MrosBo00/gamelog/1990/ |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> Mrosko was waived on August 26, 1991.<ref name="pst">{{Cite web |title=Search Results |url=https://www.prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Bob+Mrosko&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search |access-date=December 27, 2024 |publisher=prosportstransactions.com}}</ref>

Mrosko was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on October 2, 1991.<ref name="transactions" /> He played in 11 games, starting four, for the Colts in 1991, recording eight receptions for 90 yards.<ref name="pfr" /> He became a free agent after the season and re-signed with the Colts.<ref name="transactions" /> He was released on August 25, 1992.<ref name="transactions" />

'''Robert Bruce Olderman''' (June 6, 1962 – October 20, 1993) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive guard]] who played one season with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the Chiefs in the fourth round of the [[1985 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] at the [[University of Virginia]].

==Early life and college==
Robert Bruce Olderman was born on June 6, 1962, in [[Brookville, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/o/olde00200.html | title=Bob Olderman | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=7 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Marist School (Georgia)|Marist School]] in [[Brookhaven, Georgia]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

Olderman was a member of the [[Virginia Cavaliers football]] team from 1980 to 1984 and a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1982 to 1984.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="death"/> He was [[redshirted]] in 1980.<ref name="death"/> His senior year in 1984, he was a team captain and was named first-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] by the [[Associated Press]].<ref name=AP>{{cite news|title=All-ACC Team|newspaper=The Mount Airy News|date=November 20, 1984 |page=7A|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=D28_AAAAIBAJ&dq=All-ACC+football+team&pg=PA4&article_id=6818,5260449}}</ref><ref name="death"/>

==Professional career==
Olderman was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the fourth round, with the 99th overall pick, of the [[1985 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OldeBo20.htm | title=Bob Olderman | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=7 December 2024}}</ref> He officially signed with the team on July 19.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in all 16 games, starting 14, for the Chiefs during his rookie year in 1985.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released on August 26, 1986.<ref name="transactions"/>

Olderman signed with the [[Denver Broncos]] on May 1, 1987.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on September 7, 1987.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/o/olde00200.html | title=Bob Olderman NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=7 December 2024}}</ref>

==Later life==
Olderman was involved in real estate in [[Atlanta, Georgia]] after his NFL career.<ref name="death"/> On October 20, 1993, in Atlanta, he died at the age of 31 from [[Castleman disease]].<ref name="death">{{Cite web |title=EX-CAV OLDERMAN DIES |url=https://scholar.lib.vt.edu/VA-news/ROA-Times/issues/1993/rt9310/931022/10220016.htm |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=scholar.lib.vt.edu}}</ref>

'''Robert A. Martin''' (born November 14, 1953) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for four seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[New York Jets]] and [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He was selected by the Jets in the sixth round of the [[1976 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]].

==Early life==
Robert A. Martin was born on November 14, 1953, in [[David City, Nebraska]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/m/mart01400.html | title=Bob Martin | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=26 December 2024}}</ref> He attended David City High School, [[letterman (sports)|lettering]] in football, basketball, track, and golf.<ref name="Pfa"/> He earned 14 varsity letters in high school.<ref name="bio"/> He played both offense and defense on the football team, initially playing [[quarterback]] before converting to [[running back]] for his final two seasons.<ref name="A"/> He was a linebacker on defense.<ref name="A"/> Martin was named first-team Central Ten All-Conference for three straight seasons in both football and basketball.<ref name="bio"/> He also earned Class C first-team all-state honors in football in 1971 and 1972.<ref name="bio"/> Martin was also a runner-up for the state [[triple jump]] twice.<ref name="bio"/> He helped David City High win state titles in football and basketball his senior season as well.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="A">{{cite web | url=https://www.huskersillustrated.com/nebraska_football/stories/seizing-the-opportunity/article_fd1d2474-b498-11ee-b6b9-5f2b4b197c99.html | title=Seizing The Opportunity | publisher=huskersillustrated.com | date=January 16, 2024 | accessdate=27 December 2024 | author=Gilster, Shane G.}}</ref> He was named the Nebraska High School Athlete of the Year by both the ''[[Lincoln Journal-Star]]'' and the ''[[Omaha World-Herald]]'' his senior year in 1972.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="A"/> He played in the Shrine Bowl all-star game after his senior year.<ref name="bio"/> Martin was inducted into the Nebraska High School Sports Hall of Fame in 2003.<ref name="bio">{{cite web | url=https://nebhalloffame.org/bob-martin-david-city/ | title=Bob Martin – David City | publisher=nebhalloffame.org | accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Martin was a member of the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] of the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] from 1972 to 1975.<ref name="Pfa"/> He started his college career as a running back on the freshman team before switching to [[defensive end]] later.<ref name="A"/> He was a three-year letterman and a stand-up defensive end from 1973 to 1975.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="jets">{{cite web | url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/where-are-they-now-bob-martin | title=Where Are They Now: Bob Martin | publisher=newyorkjets.com | date=April 1, 2021 | accessdate=27 December 2024 | author=Gehman, Jim}}</ref> Martin started every game as a sophomore in 1973, recording 65 tackles and two fumble recoveries.<ref name="A"/> He garnered [[Associated Press]] (AP) first-team All-[[Big Eight Conference]] honors his junior year in 1974 and AP and [[United Press International]] first-team All-Big Eight honors his senior year in 1975.<ref>{{cite news|title=Humm Leads Cornhusker Contingent on AP All-Big Eight|newspaper=Lincoln (NE) Journal|date=November 29, 1974|page=17|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/7229346/humm_leads_cornhusker_contingent_on_ap/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=All-Big Eight team|newspaper=Greeley (CO) Daily Tribune|date=November 21, 1975|page=35|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/2826609/pete_brock_21_nov_1975_allbig_eight/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Three players unanimous choices for all-Big Eight football honors|newspaper=The Telegraph-Herald|date=November 25, 1975|page=12|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OvZQAAAAIBAJ&dq=1975+All-Big+Eight+Conference+football+team+upi&pg=PA7&article_id=5028,4306220}}</ref> He was named a second-team [[All-American]] by the AP in both 1974 and 1975,<ref>{{cite news|title=USC Star All-America 3rd Time; 3 SWC Players Named On Defense|newspaper=The Corpus Christi Times|date=December 6, 1974|page=10B|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4489865/usc_star_allamerican_3rd_time/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=OSU places two on All-America list|newspaper=The Xenia Daily Gazette|date=December 2, 1975|page=7|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4496661/osu_places_two_on_allamerica_list/}}</ref> a second-team All-American by UPI in 1975,<ref>{{cite news|title=Griffin earns All America honors third straight year|newspaper=The Pocono Record|date=December 4, 1975|page=15|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4496950/griffin_earns_all_america_honors_third/}}</ref> and a first-team All-American by ''Football News'' in 1975.<ref name=FN>{{cite news|title=Buckeyes, Sooners Head Football News Team|newspaper=Kingsport (TN) Times|date=November 27, 1975|page=7C|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4497459/buckeyes_sooners_head_football_news/}}</ref> He was also a team co-captain his senior season.<ref name="bio"/> Martin played in the [[Hula Bowl]] and [[Japan Bowl]] after his senior year.<ref name="A"/>

==Professional career==
Martin was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the sixth round, with the 163rd overall pick, of the [[1976 NFL draft]].<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MartBo20.htm | title=Bob Martin | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref> He played in 13 games, all starts at linebacker, for the Jets during the 1976 season, recording two interceptions.<ref name="pfr"/><ref name="jets"/> He started the first five games of the season in 1977 and made one interception before being placed on injured reserve with a separated shoulder on October 25, 1977.<ref name="pfr"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MartBo20/gamelog/1977/ | title=Bob Martin 1977 Game Log | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="jets"/><ref name="transactions"/> Martin started all 16 games for the Jets in 1978, totaling 2.5 sacks and two interceptions.<ref name="pfr"/> The Jets finished the year with an 8–8 record.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyj/1978.htm | title=1978 New York Jets | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref> He started the first two games of the 1979 season before being released on September 19, 1979, after a contract dispute.<ref name="pfr"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MartBo20/gamelog/1979/ | title=Bob Martin 1979 Game Log | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/><ref name="jets"/>

Martin was claimed off waivers by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on September 20, 1979.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 13 games, starting two, for the 49ers in 1979, recording one fumble recovery.<ref name="pfr"/> He was released on June 4, 1980.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/m/mart01400.html | title=Bob Martin NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
After his NFL career, Martin spent time working for [[Valmont Industries]], including stints as a product development manager and national sales manager.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="jets"/> His daughter Anne and son Lee were on the Cornhuskers track team while another son Jay played football for the Cornhuskers.<ref name="A"/>

'''Robert Picard''' (born November 24, 1949) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for three years in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Seattle Seahawks]] and [[Detroit Lions]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|Eastern Washington Eagles]].

==College career==
Picard walked on to [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|Eastern Washington State]], which is now known as Eastern Washington. He played four years as a wide receiver, setting career records for catches (166), yards (2,373), and touchdowns (19). These marks stood for 22 years until they were broken in 1993. He had his number 84 jersey retired, making him one of only two players to have received this honor at Eastern Washington, the other being [[Michael Roos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cheneyfreepress.com/story/2013/12/19/sports/walk-on-bob-picard-helped-pave-the-nfl-road-at-eastern/13101.html |title=Walk-on Bob Picard helped pave the NFL road at Eastern |publisher=Cheney Free Press |date=|accessdate=April 30, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Picard was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the sixth round of the [[1973 NFL draft]]. He spent three seasons with the Eagles, making his mark primarily on special teams. He was selected in the [[1976 NFL expansion draft]] by the [[Seattle Seahawks]], but he was cut in training camp. He then returned to the Philadelphia Eagles for four games before being traded mid-season to the [[Detroit Lions]], where he would play the final eight games of his career.

Picard never caught a regular season pass in the NFL, but his play on special teams was renowned. One Philadelphia sportswriter once said of Picard that "''Of all the Philadelphia Eagles, the easiest one to find in the locker room is Bobby Picard. He's the one covered with all the blood. Number 82 in your program, but No. 1 in the kamikaze ranks. The guy who looks like a walking transfusion.''"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://goeags.com/hof.aspx?hof=50&path=&kiosk= |title=Bob Picard - EWU athletics hall of fame |publisher=goeags.com |date=|accessdate=April 30, 2017}}</ref>

'''Robert E. Otto''' (born December 12, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Houston Oilers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Idaho State Bengals football|Idaho State Bengals]].

==Early life==
Otto attended [[Foothill High School (Sacramento, California)|Foothill High School]], where he played [[tight end]]. He accepted a football scholarship from [[Idaho State University]], where he was converted into a [[defensive end]]. He started a few games as a sophomore. He became a regular starter as a junior.

He registered 45 tackles (6 for loss) as a senior. He finished his college career with 145 tackles (21 for loss).

==Professional career==
===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
Otto was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the ninth round (248th overall) of the [[1985 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite book |title=The ESPN Pro Football Encyclopedia |date=2007 |publisher=Sterling Publishing |isbn=978-1-4027-4216-3 |page=[https://archive.org/details/espnprofootballe00ster/page/552 552] |edition=first |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/espnprofootballe00ster/page/552 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1985 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |access-date=October 5, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
In [[1986 NFL season|1986]], he signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He was released on September 1, [[1986 NFL season|1986]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/09/02/sports/transactions-801886.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=September 2, 1986 | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was signed on September 23, to replace [[defensive end]] [[Jesse Baker (American football)|Jesse Baker]].<ref>{{cite web | title=The Dallas Cowboys Tuesday re-signed cornerback Manny Hendrix, who... | website=UPI | date=1986-09-23 | url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1986/09/23/The-Dallas-Cowboys-Tuesday-re-signed-cornerback-Manny-Hendrix-who/9402527832000/ | access-date=2025-10-23}}</ref> He wasn't re-signed after the season.

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On April 3, [[1987 NFL season|1987]], he signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 3, 1987 |title=The Seattle Seahawks announced the signing of four free... |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1987/04/03/The-Seattle-Seahawks-announced-the-signing-of-four-free/4755544424400/ |access-date=January 12, 2019 |website=UPI.com}}</ref> He was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on September 1, before being cut later in September.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/09/02/sports/transactions-906687.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=September 2, 1987 | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Houston Oilers===
In September [[1987 NFL season|1987]], he signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Houston Oilers]]. He was released on October 27.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/10/28/sports/transactions-438287.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=October 28, 1987 | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

'''Bob Lingenfelter''' (born September 1, 1954 – January 29, 2025)<ref name=":0">https://www.norfolkneradio.com/news/bob-lingenfelter-passes-away/article_a6b03d8a-df1f-11ef-b199-cfa162133051.html</ref> was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|tackle]] and [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]]. He played for the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 1977 and for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LingBo20.htm |title=Bob Lingenfelter Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |date= |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/boblingenfelter/2519545/profile |title=Bob Lingenfelter, T |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

== High school and college career ==
Lingenfelter attended Plainview High School, he gathered all-conference and all-state honors in football, while also finishing as the state runner-up heavyweight wrestler and setting school records in shot put and discus for the track team.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Robert Lingenfelter Obituary January 29, 2025 |url=https://www.snidermemorialfh.com/obituaries/robert-lingenfelter |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Snider Memorial Funeral Home |language=en}}</ref>

Lingenfelter then enjoyed a standout college football career playing for his home state [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]], earning second-team [[All-Big Eight Conference football teams|All-Big Eight]] honors as a junior in 1975 and first-team All-Big Eight and honorable mention [[All-America|All-American honors]] as a senior.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Bob Lingenfelter - Football 1976 |url=https://huskers.com/sports/football/roster/player/bob-lingenfelter |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=University of Nebraska - Official Athletics Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Pro career ==
Lingenfelter was picked in the 7th round of the [[1977 NFL draft|1977 NFL Draft]] by the [[Cleveland Browns]]. He played 14 games for the Browns in 1977, starting two. He played five games in 1978 for the [[Minnesota Vikings]].

== Personal ==
Following his football career, Lingenfelter returned to Plainview to work as a farmer.<ref name=":1" />

In 2012, Lingenfelter ran as a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] in the U.S. House primary to represent [[Nebraska's 3rd congressional district|Nebraska's 3rd District]]. He lost to incumbent U.S. Representative [[Adrian Smith (politician)|Adrian Smith]] 81.4% to 18.6%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Lingenfelter |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Bob_Lingenfelter |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=GUENTHER |first=JERRY |date=2012-03-30 |title=Dissatisfaction prompts Plainview man to run for Congress |url=https://norfolkdailynews.com/news/dissatisfaction-prompts-plainview-man-to-run-for-congress/article_ddf8ec96-7a70-11e1-ae46-001a4bcf6878.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=The Norfolk Daily News |language=en}}</ref>

Lingenfelter worked for [[WJAG|WJAG News Talk radio]] (780 AM) out of [[Norfolk, Nebraska]], as an on-air market analyst.<ref name=":0" />

Lingenfelter's father played on the freshman team at Nebraska, while his son Newton was a walk-on who earned a scholarship in 2005 and his nephew Ben also played for the Huskers. Another of Lingenfelter's sons, Harrison, played college football at University of Nebraska Omaha.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Babcock |first=Mike |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Heart_of_a_Husker/ikyie5548-0C?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Bob+Lingenfelter&pg=PA14&printsec=frontcover |title=Heart of a Husker: Tom Osborne's Nebraska Legacy |date=2006 |publisher=Sports Publishing LLC |isbn=978-1-59670-017-8 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Service |first=World-Herald News |date=2017-02-06 |title=Yet another Lingenfelter to be part of Husker football program |url=https://norfolkdailynews.com/news/yet-another-lingenfelter-to-be-part-of-husker-football-program/article_0f541ac8-ec7b-11e6-926b-17e6e4145c66.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=The Norfolk Daily News |language=en}}</ref>

Lingenfelter was inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame in 2006.<ref name=":2" /> He was also inducted into the Plainview High School Hall of Fame in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plainview Public Schools - Plainview High School Hall of Fame Class of 2021 |url=https://www.plainviewschools.org/vnews/display.v/ART/622126593c55c |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.plainviewschools.org |language=en}}</ref>

Lingenfelter died of a heart attack on January 29, 2025.<ref>[https://www.snidermemorialfh.com/obituaries/robert-lingenfelter Robert Lingenfelter]</ref>

'''Robert E. McDonough''' (born March 7, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/m/mcdo05000.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Bob McDonough Stats}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/m/mcdo05000.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Bob McDonough NFL Transactions}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[California Vulcans football|California Vulcans]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McDoBo21.htm | title=Bob McDonough stats |access-date=June 11, 2024 |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob McDonough, DB |url= https://www.nfl.com/players/bob-mcdonough/ |access-date=June 11, 2024 |work=Nfl.com}}</ref>

A native of [[Pittsburgh]], McDonough attended [[Perry Traditional Academy High School]] but did not play football. He then attended [[Pennsylvania Western University, California]], and after a successful tryout for the football team, was a starter all four years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-post-gazette/149174556/|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 28, 1986|page=46|title=Four-year college starter didn't play football at Perry|author=Stempler, Steve}} {{Open access}}</ref> He tried out with the NFL's [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] after not being selected in the [[1987 NFL draft]], but was not signed. During the [[1987 NFL strike]], he was signed by the [[Detroit Lions]], for whom he played [[Nickelback (American football)|nickelback]] and on [[special teams]], later being released after the three-game strike ended. He then played in a Pittsburgh-area minor league; the ''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'' noted that within a month he went from covering all-time great [[Steve Largent]] to "receivers in the Greater Pittsburgh Football League, receivers whose names will never be the stuff of which the NFL marquees are made."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-post-gazette/149174695/|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 12, 1987|page=18|title=Perry's McDonough plays closer to home after NFL stint|author=Tuma, Gary}} {{Open access}}</ref>

'''Robert Morris Simpson''' (born March 29, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Miami Dolphins]] for five games in 1978. He played [[college football]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado Buffaloes]].<ref>https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SimpBo20.htm</ref>

==Professional career==
Simpson was selected by the Miami Dolphins in the eighth round (the 230th pick) of the [[1976 NFL draft]] out of the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] before being released in training camp. He was resigned by the team in the offseason before the 1978 season started.

'''Robert Earl Meeks Jr.''' (born May 28, 1969) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Denver Broncos]], the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[Baltimore Stallions]] and the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF) for the [[Barcelona Dragons (NFL Europe)|Barcelona Dragons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Meeks Football Statistics {{!}} The Football Database |url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/bob-meeks-meeksbo01 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=FootballDB.com |language=en}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Meeks Stats, News and Video - C |url=https://www.nfl.com/players/bob-meeks/ |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=[[NFL.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Meeks Biography |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/bio/_/id/7295/bob-meeks |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Meeks - Football 1991 |url=https://auburntigers.com/sports/football/roster/player/bob-meeks |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=[[Auburn Tigers]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Denver Broncos ===
Meeks was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the tenth round, with the 278th overall pick, of the [[1992 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=2024-04-14 |title=Auburn’s NFL Draft: ‘Captain Crunch’ and the outsiders |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2024/04/auburns-nfl-draft-captain-crunch-and-the-outsiders.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240423220309/https://www.al.com/sports/2024/04/auburns-nfl-draft-captain-crunch-and-the-outsiders.html |archive-date=23 Apr 2024 |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=al |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-21 |title=Denver Broncos - 1992 Draft Picks |url=https://www.retroseasons.com/teams/denver-broncos/1992/draft-picks/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710003225/https://www.retroseasons.com/teams/denver-broncos/1992/draft-picks/ |archive-date=2025-07-10 |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=RetroSeasons |language=en-US}}</ref> He officially signed with the team on July 17 but did not appear in any games for the Broncos during the [[1992 Denver Broncos season|1992 season]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Bob Meeks Transactions - Pro Football Archives |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/m/meek00400.html |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=www.profootballarchives.com}}</ref>

The [[1993 Denver Broncos season|1993 season]] saw his first game appearance in the Week 1 game with a win against the [[1993 New York Jets season|New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Meeks 1993 Game Logs {{!}} The Football Database |url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/bob-meeks-meeksbo01/gamelogs/1993 |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=FootballDB.com |language=en}}</ref> He played in the first eight games of the season for the Broncos and recorded one kick return for nine yards in a win against the [[1993 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 4.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Broncos 35-13 Colts (Oct 3, 1993) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore/_/gameId/131003007 |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[1994 Denver Broncos season|1994 season]], on August 23, Meeks was placed on injured reserve and missed the entire season. He was released on July 11, 1995 and then signed with Broncos again on July 12.<ref name=":0" /> Meeks was released again on August 22, ahead of the start of the [[1995 Denver Broncos season|1995 season]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Baltimore Stallions ===
Meeks would be signed by the [[Baltimore Stallions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on September 5, 1995, where they would win the [[83rd Grey Cup]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Barcelona Dragons ===
Meeks was selected by the [[Barcelona Dragons (ELF)|Barcelona Dragons]] with the 22nd pick in the fourth round of the 1996 WLAF draft.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Official 1996 World League of American Football Fact Book |pages=146–147 |chapter=1996 Round by Round Draft}}</ref> He would make the final roster for the [[1996 Barcelona Dragons season|Dragons]] as a center.<ref name="1996 WLAF Fact Book">{{cite book |title=The Official 1996 World League of American Football Fact Book |pages=20–27 |chapter=Barcelona Dragons}}</ref>
